threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local Rust document-processing engine for DOCX comparison, tracked edits, revision settlement, inspection, validation, scrubbing, Markdown conversion and PDF/PNG rendering. Rust CLI, Python/PyO3 and WASM interfaces share engine code; Python and Node add their own local filesystem adapters. The optional Python MCP server exposes document tools over stdio and grants a persistent directory capability rooted at --root, defaulting to the server working directory. Native rendering additionally accesses host font resources and a persistent font index. Explicit self-update and maintainer release/review automation have separate network, credential and publication authority. This is a source-backed architecture map, not completed security-audit coverage. Evidence: Cargo.toml:57-58, Cargo.toml:102-128, src/lib.rs:96-165, jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:43-49, jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-37, jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-19, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381.
assets: Confidential input documents, document text, comments, authorship and revision history; derived clean/redline DOCX files, Markdown patches, JSON reports and rendered PDF/PNG artifacts. MCP edit writes <root>/<out_dir>/clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff and report.json, with optional redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:152-205.

Integrity of caller-selected local files and the MCP server's granted document directory. The directory capability is held open, while ambient CLI publication intentionally accepts local paths outside any common root. Evidence: src/publication.rs:146-217.

Host memory and CPU used by archive decompression, XML parsing, document comparison, legacy DOC parsing, fonts, image decoding and rendering. Default admission limits are 64 MiB compressed, 10,000 entries, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB inflated and XML depth 256; comparison limits raise compressed/per-part bounds to 512 MiB and aggregate inflated bytes to 2 GiB. Evidence: src/admission.rs:39-100.

Native renderer font files and persistent index metadata. The index defaults to ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or ~/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Linux, and %APPDATA%\jubarte\font-index.tsv on Windows; JUBARTE_FONT_DIR changes its default parent and JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides or disables it. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652, src/convert/font.rs:3098-3107, src/convert/font.rs:3182-3229.

Installed CLI executable, release archives/checksums, package-registry identities and publication credentials. Current updater trusted signing keys are empty and the first signed release is unset. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48, src/update.rs:198-258, scripts/release.sh:374-380, scripts/release.sh:919-959, scripts/release.sh:1063-1069.

GitHub release-write authority, optional release signing private key, Jules API credentials and delegated review/remediation capabilities. These are privileged development workflows, separate from document processing. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:230-307, .github/workflows/release.yml:356-369, .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-41, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324.
trustBoundaries: Document producer -> Rust package/XML consumers: caller-controlled ZIP records, part names, compressed data and XML cross into trusted process memory. Admission checks central/local ZIP consistency, special-entry defects, case-folded duplicate names, encryption/compression policy, streamed inflated-byte budgets and XML checks. InputLimitOverrides rejects unknown configuration fields. Evidence: src/admission.rs:103-138, src/admission.rs:439-553, src/opc/archive.rs:34-51. The library forbids unsafe Rust in its own code: src/lib.rs:86.

Library caller -> raw XML parser: parse_xdocument is intentionally permissive and allocates a character vector without applying input policy; try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before constructing its DOM. Callers choosing the raw API own prior admission and process limits. Evidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:88-135. Default tag limits are 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte qualified attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-57.

Legacy DOC producer -> legacy parser: supported conversion follows the separate compound-file/WordDocument/FIB/table pipeline rather than DOCX ZIP admission. Stream structure and encryption checks belong to legacy_doc, and process resource limits remain a host obligation. Evidence: src/legacy_doc.rs:174-216, src/legacy_doc.rs:765-795.

Edit-plan producer -> document transaction: version-1 source SHA-256 is checked when supplied; version-2 source SHA-256 is mandatory and checked after plan validation. Version-1 editing refuses packages containing XML signatures or vbaProject.bin. These integrity checks bind source bytes, not authenticated identity or human approval. Evidence: src/edit.rs:2072-2104, src/edit/v2_apply.rs:75-100.

MCP client -> document filesystem: all connected clients receive the tools installed by build_server, with document reads/publication mediated by _native._OutputRoot and cap_std::fs::Dir. --root defaults to Path.cwd(); expanded/resolved root is opened once. Python resolution checks provide diagnostics, while actual reads and writes use the persistent capability. No per-user authentication or tenant partition is implemented by this stdio adapter. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381, jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276, src/publication.rs:146-199.

MCP mutation -> output publication: output paths must pass portable-relative-name validation; target symlinks/directories are refused, and overwrite=false uses atomic hard-link installation. All bytes are staged and verified before any commit; atomicity is per file, and errors can report an already committed subset. Unix staging directories use mode 0700; Windows inherits platform access controls. Evidence: src/publication.rs:83-143, src/publication.rs:168-199, src/publication.rs:228-245, src/publication.rs:431-512, src/publication.rs:535-570.

Local CLI caller -> ambient filesystem: native publish_paths holds destination-parent handles and stages outputs, but deliberately grants ambient local-path authority. Python CLI _write uses Path.write_bytes; Node CLI write uses fs.writeFileSync. Their preflight existence checks are distinct from native publication enforcement and must be reviewed independently. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273, src/publication.rs:203-225, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-103, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-79, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111.

Markdown image names -> native CLI resource loader: the trusted root is explicit --resource-path or the Markdown file's parent, falling back to '.'. URL schemes are refused, percent escapes are decoded before policy checks, canonicalized targets must remain under the root, and actual reads use OutputRoot. The general Markdown library instead accepts a caller-provided image callback, absent by default. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878, src/bin/jubarte.rs:2936-2943, src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198, src/markdown/mod.rs:216-226.

Document font requests -> ambient native font discovery/index: document family names select parsed host fonts, including system, Word and cloud-cache locations and configured user fonts. Cloud-family names must be one normal path component. The persistent index records source paths and timestamps, reloads matching files and saves through a process-specific temporary filename followed by rename. These operations do not use the MCP OutputRoot. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236, src/convert/font.rs:2263-2315, src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652, src/convert/font.rs:3154-3172, src/convert/font.rs:3182-3229.

Operator -> updater -> installed executable: explicit self-update resolves releases from jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, selects one platform archive and inner jubarte binary, requires checksum verification and registers an extracted-regular-file verification hook. Noninteractive installation needs --yes; --check only resolves availability; explicitly requested versions can downgrade. Signature verification is implemented but inactive with the current empty key list. Extraction, HTTP behavior and executable replacement are delegated to self_update and were not independently inspected here. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48, src/update.rs:88-124, src/update.rs:144-161, src/update.rs:186-258, src/update.rs:307-321.

Maintainer/CI -> release consumers: tag-driven GitHub builds have contents:read, while the release job alone has contents:write. Optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY reaches the signing step and temporary $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN files; checksums are generated after signing. A separate local release script can publish crates.io, two npm packages, PyPI and a GitHub fallback release using operator credentials. Its typed version confirmation can be bypassed with the explicit --yes option, and security-check.sh runs even with --skip-gates. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-25, .github/workflows/release.yml:51-89, .github/workflows/release.yml:230-321, scripts/release.sh:374-380, scripts/release.sh:655-660, scripts/release.sh:875-899, scripts/release.sh:919-959, scripts/release.sh:976-1012, scripts/release.sh:1039-1069.

PR content -> privileged review/remediation automation: one pinned reviewer receives JULES_API_KEY and a GitHub token with contents:read, pull-requests:write and checks:write, gated to same-repository non-Dependabot PRs, without local checkout. A different pinned companion-remediation action receives JULES_API_KEY and starts only for trusted arthrod author/dispatcher conditions; its requested mode is AUTO_CREATE_PR with require_plan_approval:false. Companion workflow document gates and prompts do not establish what the external action or Jules service enforces. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-50, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:46-54, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:65-102, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can control DOCX ZIP/XML, embedded media/fonts, Markdown text/image references or supported legacy DOC bytes that a caller elects to process. They do not thereby control trusted process environment, CLI arguments, MCP root selection, host filesystem permissions or release credentials.

An MCP client can invoke the registered read/write tools and select paths within the operator-granted root, including overwrite=true. All clients sharing this server share that capability; a meaningful boundary failure would add access outside that grant, rather than merely exercise permitted edits. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:152-168.

A library caller may supply permissive XML, increased limits or an image callback; those choices are caller authority, not proof that an untrusted document can alter policy. Resource-exhaustion impact on a shared service requires a host deployment and workload access not supplied here. Evidence: src/admission.rs:103-164, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:88-135, src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198.

A release-asset attacker would need write access to release artifacts or a separate transport/provider compromise. The current checksum-only updater cannot distinguish coordinated archive/checksum replacement using an independent signing identity, as the documentation explicitly explains. Evidence: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80, src/update.rs:44-48.

PR authors control reviewed source and PR metadata within their GitHub permissions. Fork authors are excluded from the privileged Jules paths inspected here; same-repository authors and the trusted companion-remediation trigger have different authority. No claim is made that PR text alone can acquire repository write authority. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-31, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:65-82, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324.
securityObjectives: Bound untrusted package/XML resource use and reject unsafe or ambiguous package representations before protected processing; preserve explicit caller-configured limits. Raw permissive parsing and maintainer debug inspection must remain distinguishable from checked admission. Evidence: src/admission.rs:39-164, src/admission.rs:439-553, src/opc/archive.rs:15-19, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:88-135.

Keep MCP document reads and publication within the persistent root capability despite symlink/path replacement, preserve overwrite opt-in and report partial publication accurately. Evidence: src/publication.rs:83-199, src/publication.rs:431-570.

Bind prepared edits to the intended source and expose refusal outcomes; do not treat a content digest, selected author string or model-visible tool annotation as authenticated authority. Evidence: src/edit.rs:2081-2092, src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-100, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55.

Prevent Markdown image references from gaining arbitrary host-file or network read authority in the native CLI loader; caller-provided library callbacks own their additional authority. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878, src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198.

Install only the explicitly selected release's intended regular executable, with the configured checksum/signature policy and operator confirmation semantics. Preserve the distinction between implemented signing support and active trusted signing keys. Evidence: src/update.rs:104-124, src/update.rs:198-258, src/update.rs:307-321.

Keep release signing, registry publication, review comments and companion PR creation as separately authorized capabilities. Bind published versions/artifacts and constrain credentials to their intended consumers. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:31-49, .github/workflows/release.yml:230-307, scripts/release.sh:875-899, .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-39, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324.
assumptions: Authorized scope is the current repository at '.', with no supplied deployment context, threat model or knowledge base. Source inspection was offline and read-only; application code and tests were not executed. Ignored dependency/build directories and the target symlink were not followed. Only root SECURITY.md was found in the nonignored source inventory.

No public web service, tenant deployment or external authentication layer was established. MCP is stdio-only in the inspected entrypoint; client authentication, subprocess sandboxing, memory/CPU quotas and filesystem ACLs remain host responsibilities. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; SECURITY.md documents process limits as a caller obligation.

Documentation/control qualification: build_server describes tools as only touching files under root, and explicit document I/O does use OutputRoot. Native render font discovery and font-index persistence instead use ambient host paths, potentially outside that root. Thus the root is a document-I/O capability boundary, not an established process-wide filesystem sandbox. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108, src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652, src/convert/font.rs:3098-3107, src/convert/font.rs:3154-3229.

Signing is staged rather than currently mandatory: docs describe signature protection after activation and explicitly disclose checksum-only operation before that point; actual RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None. No deployed secret or release state was queried. Evidence: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-87, src/update.rs:44-48.

The local release fallback assembles downloaded CI artifacts and directly creates a release after checksumming, without the release workflow's signing block. Current empty trusted keys make this compatible with current updater policy; behavior after future signing activation needs separate review. Evidence: scripts/release.sh:976-1012, .github/workflows/release.yml:252-307, src/update.rs:44-48.

Dependency documentation has drifted: SECURITY.md discusses rdocx-opc 0.2 and quick-xml 0.41; the inspected manifest actually names oxml-opc 0.14.2, direct quick-xml 0.42 and a separate 0.41 alias for OPC error compatibility. Treat the manifest/lockfile dependency graph as current implementation evidence rather than assuming the older package name describes it. Evidence: Cargo.toml:131-149.

self_update implementation, external pinned GitHub actions, Jules service authorization and the external app release-engine.sh are not present in the inspected source surfaces. Their endpoint credential forwarding, extraction/replacement mechanics, actual branch-write grants and publication approval controls remain unresolved. Evidence: src/update.rs:198-258, .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:35-41, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:272-324, scripts/release.sh:382-389.

The general Python Document facade stores bytes without parsing on construction; native operations perform validation. Loading a Document is therefore not itself proof of admission. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:116-145.

Native, Python and Node CLIs share engine semantics but not a single filesystem writer. Do not infer native staged publication guarantees for Python Path.write_bytes or Node fs.writeFileSync. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111.

scope.summary: Current repository; architecture mapping is not full source-audit coverage.

findings.title: Tiny Markdown table metadata can trigger unbounded cell allocation
findings.summary: A caller-controlled cells paragraph range is converted into an unbounded count and used to append padding cells. A tiny Markdown table with a range such as p0-p1000000000 causes roughly a billion padding entries to be allocated before DOCX assembly, exhausting CPU and memory in Rust, Python, or WASM conversion hosts.

severity.rationale: A small untrusted Markdown input can exhaust or terminate its processing host. Reachability is direct through public byte/string APIs; remote or multi-user service exposure is conditional, and there is no confidentiality or integrity compromise.
severity.changeConditions: Process memory/CPU limits and worker isolation constrain impact; a shared remotely exposed conversion service would increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source tracing establishes the unchecked numeric count, default public conversion path, and count-driven Vec growth; runtime exhaustion was deliberately not executed.

codeEvidence.label: Table cell range has no amplification bound
codeEvidence.explanation: Checked arithmetic prevents overflow but accepts arbitrarily large representable cell counts.

codeEvidence.label: Declared count directly drives vector growth
codeEvidence.explanation: For a table row without break markers, padding grows until the attacker-selected n; actual Markdown cells do not bound it.

codeEvidence.label: Public conversion calls parser before output assembly
codeEvidence.explanation: Normal valid conversion options reach read(), whose line 155 computes table_plans before event-level view filtering.

codeEvidence.label: Sibling paragraph range already has an explicit limit
codeEvidence.explanation: MOST_EMPTY exists but is not applied to row_paragraphs.

rootCause.summary: Table metadata range parsing omits the existing per-range bound and the table planner trusts the resulting count for allocation.

findings.remediation: Validate row_paragraphs with the same bounded range helper used elsewhere, impose a total table/output cell budget before allocation, and return a structured refusal rather than silently processing an oversized range.

counterEvidence: checked_sub and checked_add reject descending/overflowing ranges but do not limit large valid ranges.
The count branch requires one metadata range per actual table row and no break marker; a single-header-row table can satisfy both.
Sibling paragraph_range caps MOST_EMPTY at 100000, but this branch does not call it.
SECURITY.md recommends process limits; these limit blast radius without preventing the input amplification.
limitations: No application code or resource-exhaustion proof was executed.
Actual remote/shared service deployment is not established.
validation.summary: Independently traced metadata collection in table_plans, checked range parsing, the no-break row branch, and Rust/Python/WASM public conversion callers. No range or output budget intervenes before padding allocation.

dataflow.summary: markdown_to_docx(markdown) -> read -> table_plans -> view_notes::table_line -> row_paragraphs count -> plan_table -> pad.push until n.

likelihood.summary: Deterministic input amplification; attacker access to a shared conversion host is deployment-dependent.

reachability.summary: Rust markdown_to_docx and Python/WASM wrappers accept caller-controlled text; ordinary valid options reach the table planner without admitting a DOCX archive first.
reachability.attacker: Document supplier to an application that converts untrusted Markdown
preconditions: The host converts attacker-supplied Markdown.
Metadata contains one range per table row, with a large valid range and no paragraph break in the affected row.

attackPath.summary: Untrusted Markdown range metadata crosses into unchecked output cardinality.

remediationTests: With a tiny one-row table, a range exceeding the configured table budget must fail promptly without allocating proportional output.
Cover valid ranges at the inclusive limit, descending/overflow ranges, multiple rows, and ranges with and without break markers across the shared public API.

findings.title: Unbounded document table spans exhaust memory during rendering
findings.summary: Untrusted DOCX table gridSpan and HTML/MHT altChunk colspan values become unrestricted output column counts. A tiny document can request a billion columns, causing layout-vector allocation or generated XML expansion before any output budget, exhausting memory and CPU despite package admission.

severity.rationale: Public render/convert APIs accept untrusted documents and a tiny accepted input produces arbitrarily large generated XML. Impact is availability of the processing host; remote/shared exposure depends on the embedding application.
severity.changeConditions: Memory/CPU-limited isolated workers constrain impact; shared conversion service exposure increases affected availability.

confidence.rationale: Source establishes package admission followed by HTML expansion, unrestricted colspan parsing, and direct count-driven XML generation; no destructive runtime proof was run.

codeEvidence.label: Colspan has no upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: A small HTML attribute can select any positive representable span.

codeEvidence.label: One output element per declared column
codeEvidence.code:
let cols = table
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.iter().map(|c| c.span).sum::<usize>())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        let col_w = 9360 / cols;
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-controlled spans become output column count.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded XML expansion loop
codeEvidence.explanation: Even a single cell can cause billions of grid elements to be allocated.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering expands relationship-selected HTML
codeEvidence.explanation: Input admission precedes expansion, so its inflated input-byte budgets do not bound generated XML.

codeEvidence.label: OOXML span accepts huge positive values
codeEvidence.explanation: Raw DOCX tables can reach the same unrestricted numeric cardinality without an altChunk.

codeEvidence.label: Span totals directly size layout vectors
codeEvidence.explanation: A tiny gridSpan value represented by a short decimal string can trigger gigabytes of column allocation.

codeEvidence.label: Merge bookkeeping also grows with span
codeEvidence.explanation: The unbounded count also propagates into merge-state allocation and iteration.

rootCause.summary: DOCX gridSpan and imported HTML colspan are trusted as output column cardinalities with only a lower bound. Both document-table paths lack a shared grid/output budget before generation and allocation.

findings.remediation: Enforce a common total table/grid budget for direct OOXML spans and HTML/MHT import before output generation or vector allocation. Reject excessive spans and use checked cumulative totals, returning a typed conversion refusal.

counterEvidence: Archive inflation and XML input limits apply to original package bytes, which can remain tiny.
The parser defaults invalid/zero spans to one but valid huge positive spans remain unrestricted.
Process resource limits recommended by SECURITY.md constrain host impact without rejecting the expansion.
limitations: No resource-exhaustion execution or observed service deployment.
validation.summary: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing. Independently verified direct OOXML gridSpan parsing (14211-14215), column occupancy allocation (13601-13615), and merge vector resize (14637-14642); they share the missing bounded table cardinality control.

dataflow.summary: DOCX main document w:altChunk r:id -> relationship target part -> chunk_html -> html_to_wml -> Builder::start(td,colspan) -> end_table cols -> XML output loop. Ordinary OOXML path: w:gridSpan/@w:val -> cell_span -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> cols allocation -> merge-state resize.

impact.summary: Processing-host memory exhaustion or prolonged CPU use.

likelihood.summary: The expansion is deterministic; exposure to untrusted callers depends on the embedding host.

reachability.summary: Public docx_to_png, render, report and PDF/layout paths call with_layout; attacker only needs to supply package bytes accepted by existing admission.
preconditions: A host renders/converts an attacker-controlled DOCX containing either a large w:gridSpan or an internal HTML/MHT chunk with a large colspan.

remediationTests: A tiny altChunk with colspan 1000000000 must fail before large output allocation.
Cover inclusive limits, cumulative spans across cells, integer overflow, nested tables, and both HTML and MHT import.
Cover direct OOXML gridSpan with tiny/no initial tblGrid, gridBefore/gridAfter variants, and merge bookkeeping as well as imported colspan.

originalCandidates.originalMessage: convert/mod.rs::cell_span lines14213-14220 parses <w:gridSpan w:val="1000000000"/> to usize with only max(1). parse_table sums raw row colspans into occupancy at13599-13604, then vec![each; occupancy]/cols.resize(occupancy,80.0) at13609-13615, later open.resize(col+span,None)14638. Suggest one broader converter table-span finding covering both OOXML gridSpan and HTML colspan; byte/XML-depth admission doesn't bound numeric expansion.

findings.title: Auxiliary XML parts bypass depth limits when named with another extension

preconditions: A rendering host imports an internal HTML/MHT chunk containing a large run of bare ampersands, which HTML text can contain.
The XML helper independently accepts arbitrary strings; package acceptance of malformed bare-ampersand XML is not required for the HTML attack.

remediationTests: Deterministic operation-count tests for long bare-ampersand runs must scale linearly.
Preserve predefined/numeric entity decoding and literal retention of unknown/truncated entities in both helpers.

originalCandidates.originalMessage: Source review has identified two availability candidates for deeper checking: xmllinq::unescape_xml_text repeatedly scans the remaining tail for ';' for each unrecognized '&' (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:764-790), while package admission ignores GeneralRef events; and drop_repeated_relationships uses repaired.contains per duplicate ID (src/opc/mod.rs:115), potentially quadratic on many pairs of distinct repeated IDs. Continuing to trace entry paths and controls. No code execution/network.
originalCandidates.siblingEvidence: Baseline: altchunk.rs::decode_entities lines723-760 also uses unbounded tail.find(';').filter(|&e| e <= 10) per ampersand. HTML chunks with many '&' and no ';' may cause quadratic scans.

surfaces.label: Markdown table metadata admission
surfaces.notes: Validated unbounded row range -> padding allocation; src/markdown/view_notes.rs:1011-1022 and src/markdown/write.rs:1265-1269. Existing MOST_EMPTY cap applies only to sibling parser.

surfaces.label: Legacy DOC overlapping text-piece amplification
surfaces.notes: Independent inspection rejects this candidate: pieces() derives adjacent CP boundaries from the same array (src/legacy_doc.rs:1092-1094), and main_text rejects any decreasing adjacent CP pair (1154-1155). This prevents the proposed repeated overlapping ranges even though coverage validation stops at the story boundary.

candidate.originalMessage: legacy_doc::main_text validates contiguous pieces only until `covered >= ccp_text` (lines1161-1175) but second pass iterates all pieces with cp_start<ccp_text (1181-1229). Repeated overlapping pieces after the first complete piece duplicate the same story bytes N times, enabling O(file_size²) memory/CPU expansion.

surfaces.label: DOCX and HTML/MHT table-span cardinality
surfaces.notes: Validated direct gridSpan allocation (src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14215,13601-13615,14637-14642) and imported colspan expansion (src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-567,469-491), consolidated under missing document-table cardinality control.

surfaces.label: Auxiliary XML parts bypass depth limits when named with another extension
surfaces.notes: Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element. Controls and counterevidence: Ordinary XML filenames and the main part are depth checked. Compressed/inflated limits still apply, but deep XML fits a small part. The raw parser is deliberately permissive; the vulnerable consumer relies on incomplete prior admission.

surfaces.label: DOCTYPE parser differential bypasses XML depth admission
surfaces.notes: DOCX main part with internal-subset comment -> admission quick-xml DocType ignored -> WmlDocument::main_document -> parse_document first-> skip -> hidden <a> strings -> recursive parse_element. Controls and counterevidence: validate_xml_with_limits rejects DTDs and protects callers that use it. Raw parse_xdocument is intentionally permissive, but WmlDocument relies on package admission. Upstream quick-xml 0.42.0 DtdParser explicitly tracks internal subsets and comments, confirming the admission side treats the hidden tags as DTD content. Input byte limits and process isolation constrain blast radius, not parser recursion.

surfaces.label: Repeated relationship IDs trigger quadratic repair work
surfaces.notes: Attacker package/part .rels -> read_relationships preserves records -> PartFs::open_within -> drop_repeated_relationships -> repeated repaired.contains string scans. Controls and counterevidence: Conflicting duplicates are rejected before the linear repair search. The 256-attribute cap is per element and does not cap the number of relationship records. Actual inflated-byte budgets bound input bytes, but permit hundreds of thousands of shallow records.

surfaces.label: Nested legacy DOC field results cause quadratic text extraction
surfaces.notes: Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops. Controls and counterevidence: Compound-file chain limits, checked stream accesses and encryption refusal protect different mechanisms. Balanced field markers satisfy normal field semantics while triggering the scan. DOCX admission later in CLI conversion does not constrain this earlier legacy extraction.

surfaces.label: Unbounded list levels cause billions of iterations or allocations
surfaces.notes: DOCX paragraph w:numPr/w:ilvl -> num_pr -> numbering lookup -> resolve_ilvl reverse integer scan; defined high levels -> next_marker lower-level counter insertion and render loop. Counterevidence: Unknown list instances return early, but the document author can define the instance. Style inheritance has a separate depth cap; it does not restrict ilvl. XML depth/tag/byte admission does not restrict this short numeric attribute.

surfaces.label: Chicago numbering counters expand one label to gigabytes
surfaces.notes: DOCX w:lvl/w:start -> NumLevel.start -> next_marker/render -> format_num(Chicago) -> chicago_label::repeat; Markdown list labels call the shared list_number formatter. Counterevidence: Alphabetic labels wrap at ALPHA_LABEL_MAX=780 and Roman labels at 32767; those related claims are rejected. The attack uses level zero, so it does not require the separate high-ilvl issue. Archive/input bounds do not bound generated marker length.

surfaces.label: Embedded font aliases retain repeated copies of one font payload
surfaces.notes: DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document. Counterevidence: Catalogue family names are skipped, but attackers can choose rare names. Invalid fonts are rejected, but a single valid font can be reused. Arc values do not deduplicate separate Vec allocations. The later u16 face-index cap occurs after font bytes have already been cloned and retained.

surfaces.label: Entity decoding repeatedly scans the input suffix
surfaces.notes: DOCX altChunk HTML text -> html_to_wml -> Builder::text -> decode_entities -> tail.find(';') per '&'; public xmllinq::unescape_xml_text similarly uses suffix.position for each unrecognized '&'. Counterevidence: The ten-character entity limit filters a found delimiter only after the expensive find. Recognized entities skip ahead, so the attack uses bare ampersands without terminating semicolons. Checked XML callers may reject malformed references; no claim is made that every checked XML package path accepts this input. Input-byte limits and process CPU quotas constrain the attack size/blast radius, but permit costly scans.

surfaces.label: Independent baseline audit
surfaces.notes: Baseline audit completed offline with source-wide searches for embedded credentials/private keys including configuration/docs/tests/examples and inactive code. No supported credential exposure was identified. This is search coverage, not full-file review for the repository. Native memory-safe crate policy does not establish dependency safety.

surfaces.label: MCP directory authority and native publication
surfaces.notes: MCP actual read/write sinks use _OutputRoot -> publication::OutputRoot -> held cap_std Dir. Portable name validation precedes write, output symlinks are refused, and overwrite=false commits via atomic hard_link. Partial publication and cleanup/durability failures are reported. src/publication.rs:83-199,228-273,431-570; mcp_server.py:67-108; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1312. Font discovery/index remains ambient and the root is not a process-wide sandbox.

surfaces.label: Markdown image file/network confinement
surfaces.notes: Native image loader decodes percent escapes before scheme/containment checks and reads through a held root capability. No source-backed traversal/SSRF bypass established. src/bin/jubarte.rs:2795-2878,2936-2943. Absolute paths resolving inside the resource root may pass despite broader comments; they add no outside-root authority.

surfaces.label: Package decompression and ZIP structure controls
surfaces.notes: Reviewed admission/archive paths check compressed/declared entries before indexing and actual streamed inflated totals. Raw local/central header names/content fields, descriptors/extents, special files and case-folded duplicate names are checked; directory payloads are charged. src/opc/archive.rs; src/admission.rs:439-575. XML policy bypasses are reported separately. Debug unchecked opener is deliberate triage behavior.

surfaces.label: External entity and relationship resolution
surfaces.notes: No local-file/network resolution was found in reviewed XML/OPC/WmlDocument paths: custom decoder recognizes only predefined/numeric entities; relationships address package parts. DTD parsing differential is an availability finding, not XXE.

surfaces.label: Updater and release credentials
surfaces.notes: Explicit updater uses fixed GitHub repository, platform binary path, checksum policy, noninteractive guard and regular-file verify hook (src/update.rs:25-48,186-321). Empty RELEASE_KEYS and None FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE mean checksum-only operation, explicitly documented in docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-87. Tag-only release signing secret is step-scoped, uses mktemp and cleanup, and verifies committed public keys; no document/PR route to signing established (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-307). Local fallback is unsigned but no active signature requirement is bypassed (scripts/release.sh:976-1033).

surfaces.label: Privileged Jules review and companion automation
surfaces.notes: Same-repository/non-Dependabot reviewer and separately trusted arthrod companion trigger are enforced in YAML. PR metadata reaches env/action inputs, with no direct shell injection established. Actual branch-write authority and prompt handling are external integration controls, not proven by YAML. .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-41; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:58-139,159-254,259-342.

surfaces.label: Python/Node ambient CLI adapters
surfaces.notes: Path.write_bytes/fs.writeFileSync differ from native staged publication, but paths come from local operator authority. No document/MCP-controlled outside-root path established. A local race story requires a hostile shared-directory writer; no differentiated authority model provided. Node consume uses O_NOFOLLOW where available and repeated descriptor/identity checks, with acknowledged lstat/unlink race requiring local writer. __main__.py:101-133; jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-111,408-552.

surfaces.label: Alphabetic and Roman label expansion
surfaces.notes: Source counterevidence rejects alpha/Roman variants: src/convert/mod.rs:6492-6505 wraps alpha at ALPHA_LABEL_MAX=780; 6508-6514 wraps Roman at 32767. Chicago lacks a corresponding bound and is reported separately.

candidate.originalMessage: Initial counter-label suspicion included alpha_label producing ~165m characters for u32::MAX.

surfaces.label: WMF/EMF coordinate amplification
surfaces.notes: Baseline reviewed coordinate/raster controls: canvas sides bound to 384, pen-width clamps, line clipping before iteration, canvas-bounded polygon fill and widened intersections defeat inspected coordinate-span candidates. This records bounded evidence, not a complete file audit of src/convert/metafile.rs.

surfaces.label: Direct gridSpan report consolidation
surfaces.notes: This candidate is validated and fully represented in resource-exhaustion.document-table-span (provenance.candidateId discovery-0008-altchunk-colspan), including original gridSpan evidence, root-control src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14215, allocation 13601-13615, and merge resize 14637-14642. Not applicable as a separate duplicate report; the vulnerability is retained, not rejected.

candidate.originalMessage: convert/mod.rs::cell_span lines14213-14220 parses <w:gridSpan w:val="1000000000"/> to usize with only max(1). parse_table sums raw row colspans into occupancy at13599-13604, then vec![each; occupancy]/cols.resize(occupancy,80.0) at13609-13615, later open.resize(col+span,None)14638. Suggest one broader converter table-span finding covering both OOXML gridSpan and HTML colspan; byte/XML-depth admission doesn't bound numeric expansion.

surfaces.label: Remaining repository source and fixtures
surfaces.notes: Full-file review is partial: 21 unique authorized files fully reviewed; 2879 remaining paths retained in coverage.deferred. Large CLI/bindings, rendering/layout, editing/comparison/revision modules, generated WASM implementation, tests/fixtures, scripts/docs/configuration retain review gaps.

deferred.reason: The Standard pass audited the listed full files and source-backed security paths, but did not fully security-audit the remaining current-scope inventory. Architecture mapping, search hits and inspected slices are not counted as completed file review.

openQuestions: Full current-scope source review remains incomplete; exact unreviewed paths are retained under discovery-0008-unreviewed-scope. Searches, architecture mapping and inspected excerpts are not completed file audits.

Runtime exploit reliability and timings were not measured; no application code, tests or PoC inputs were executed under this read-only offline audit. No smoke test was run because the audit procedure prohibits application execution.
No external shared/remote document deployment, tenant boundary, host process quotas or filesystem ACLs were supplied.
Generated WASM binaries and their consumers were not fully inspected as implementation data; native Rust findings apply to source wrappers but exact shipped-binary parity is unresolved.

Dependency-owned self_update networking/extraction/replacement and cap_std platform confinement internals, external pinned Jules actions/service authorization, and external app release-engine.sh were not fully reviewed. No network was used to retrieve them.

Same-repository PR code runs cargo clippy before the companion secret-bearing action. A meaningful gate-bypass finding needs an attacker with branch source-write authority but without executing-workflow or secret-invocation authority; that permission model is not established.

Checked package acceptance of malformed bare-ampersand XML remains unproven; the entity-decoding finding is supported through HTML altChunk text and the public XML helper rather than claiming all checked XML consumers accept it.
